title: Linkability of continuous sensor telemetry to user identity
description: Continuous GPS position, timestamps, and activity data captured by the wearable device can be linked to the specific user (EE1), enabling tracking of movements and behaviors over time.

title: Identifiability through location and health data
description: The combination of GPS position, timestamps, and heart rate data can uniquely identify the user (EE1), especially when cross-referenced with other data sources.

title: Disclosure of sensitive health and location information
description: Heart rate, step counts, and GPS position data are sensitive personal information that could be disclosed to unauthorized parties through data breaches, unauthorized access, or improper sharing.

title: Excessive data collection beyond necessity
description: Continuous collection of all sensor telemetry (heart rate, step counts, GPS, timestamps) may exceed what is necessary for the device's intended function, violating data minimization principles.

title: Usurpation of user identity through biometric data
description: Heart rate and activity patterns could potentially be used to impersonate or authenticate as the user (EE1) without proper authorization.

title: Identification from GPS Traces and Device ID
description: GPS traces and device IDs transmitted from the wearable device can be used to identify the user's location patterns and device ownership, potentially revealing personal identity and movement history.
assumptions: GPS data is accurate and device ID is unique to the user

title: Linkability Across Data Sources
description: Exercise session data, GPS traces, and timestamps from the wearable device can be linked with other data sources (e.g., health records, social media, other apps) to create comprehensive user profiles.
assumptions: Data from multiple sources can be correlated

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Sensitive Data
description: Exercise sessions, GPS traces, and device IDs stored in the companion app could be disclosed to unauthorized parties through app vulnerabilities, data breaches, or improper access controls.
assumptions: App has security vulnerabilities or inadequate access controls

title: Data Manipulation During Transmission
description: Sensor data (exercise sessions, GPS traces, timestamps) could be altered, tampered with, or corrupted during transmission from the wearable device to the companion app.
assumptions: Transmission channel is not fully secure or authenticated

title: Unauthorized Access to Companion App
description: Unauthorized individuals could gain access to the companion app and view or manipulate the user's sensitive health and location data without proper authentication.
assumptions: App authentication mechanisms are weak or compromised

title: Linkability of Health Data Across Sources
description: User's calorie, meal, and weight data logged in the companion app could be linked with other data sources (e.g., location data, purchase history, fitness tracker data) to create a comprehensive profile of the user's lifestyle and health behaviors.

title: Identifiability Through Health Data
description: The combination of calorie intake, meal details, and weight entries could be used to identify the specific user, especially when combined with other identifiers or when the data is shared with third parties.

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Sensitive Health Data
description: Personal health data (calories, meals, weight) could be disclosed to unauthorized third parties through data breaches, improper data sharing, or inadequate access controls in the companion app.

title: Usurpation of User Identity
description: An unauthorized person could gain access to the companion app and impersonate the user to log false calorie, meal, or weight entries, potentially leading to inaccurate health tracking and privacy violations.

title: Excessive Data Collection
description: The companion app may be collecting more detailed health data than necessary for its stated purpose, potentially including unnecessary personal information that increases privacy risk.

title: Linkability of Health Logs to Individuals
description: Health logs written by the companion mobile app could be linked to specific individuals through device identifiers, user accounts, or metadata, enabling tracking of individual health behaviors over time.
assumptions: The app maintains user accounts and device identifiers that can be correlated with health log entries.

title: Identifiability Through Health Log Content
description: Health logs containing calorie intake, weight history, and exercise sessions could be used to identify specific users, especially when combined with other data sources or through pattern analysis.
assumptions: Health data patterns are unique enough to identify individuals, and logs may be accessible to third parties.

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Health Logs
description: Health logs stored in the health log store could be disclosed to unauthorized parties through data breaches, improper access controls, or insider threats, exposing sensitive personal health information.
assumptions: The data store may have insufficient access controls or encryption, and health data is considered sensitive under privacy regulations.

title: Modification of Health Log Data
description: Health logs in the data store could be tampered with, altered, or deleted by unauthorized actors, compromising data integrity and potentially leading to incorrect health assessments or insurance issues.
assumptions: The data store may lack adequate integrity controls, and health logs are valuable targets for manipulation.

title: Usurpation of User Identity for Health Log Access
description: Unauthorized actors could potentially impersonate legitimate users to access or manipulate health logs through weak authentication mechanisms or credential theft.
assumptions: Authentication mechanisms may be insufficient, and health log access requires user credentials.

title: Non-compliance with Privacy Regulations
description: Collection and storage of health logs may violate privacy regulations such as GDPR or HIPAA if proper consent, data minimization, and security measures are not implemented.
assumptions: Health data is classified as sensitive personal data under privacy laws, and the app may not have adequate compliance measures.

title: Linkability of Location Traces
description: GPS location traces with timestamps can be linked to identify patterns in user movement, potentially revealing routines, frequent locations, and associations with other entities.
assumptions: Location data is stored in a format that allows temporal and spatial correlation

title: Inference of Sensitive Information
description: Location history can be analyzed to infer sensitive information such as home address, workplace, religious sites, medical facilities, political affiliations, or health conditions based on visit patterns.
assumptions: Location data is sufficient to make inferences about user activities and affiliations

title: Unauthorized Access to Location Data
description: Location history store may be accessible by unauthorized parties through network interception, insider threats, or inadequate access controls, leading to privacy violations.
assumptions: Data store has potential exposure to unauthorized access vectors

title: Tampering with Location Records
description: Location history data could be altered, deleted, or falsified by malicious actors, compromising the integrity of the data and potentially enabling fraud or denial of service.
assumptions: Data store lacks adequate integrity controls and audit mechanisms

title: Usurpation of User Identity
description: An attacker could potentially impersonate the user to access or manipulate location history data, either by compromising the app or exploiting authentication weaknesses.
assumptions: Authentication mechanisms may be vulnerable to identity spoofing

title: Health Log Data Identifiability Risk
description: The Health Analytics Service processes calorie, weight, and exercise logs that contain personally identifiable health information. Even with anonymization attempts, the combination of health metrics across multiple sessions could enable re-identification of individuals through pattern matching or cross-referencing with other data sources.
assumptions: Analytics service has access to complete historical health data across sessions

title: Unauthorized Health Data Disclosure
description: The analytics service may inadvertently or maliciously disclose sensitive health information to unauthorized parties, including through improper logging, data breaches, or unauthorized API access. Health-condition analysis data is highly sensitive and protected under regulations like HIPAA and GDPR.
assumptions: Analytics service has network access and data transmission capabilities

title: Health Data Linkability Across Sessions
description: Multiple sessions of health logs (calorie, weight, exercise) can be linked together to create a comprehensive health profile of an individual. This linkability enables tracking of health trends and behaviors over time, potentially revealing sensitive health conditions or lifestyle patterns.
assumptions: Data is stored with session identifiers that can be correlated

title: Health Data Manipulation Risk
description: The analytics service could potentially alter, tamper with, or manipulate health log data during processing. This could affect the accuracy of health-condition analysis and potentially lead to incorrect medical insights or recommendations.
assumptions: Analytics service has write access or data modification capabilities

title: Regulatory Compliance Violation Risk
description: Processing health-condition analysis data may violate privacy regulations such as HIPAA, GDPR, or other health data protection laws if proper consent, data minimization, and security measures are not implemented. Health data is a special category requiring enhanced protection.
assumptions: Analytics service processes data without adequate regulatory safeguards

title: Location History Linkability
description: Location history data from DS2 can be linked to specific individuals across multiple sessions, enabling tracking of movements and associations between different locations and time periods.
assumptions: Location data contains sufficient granularity to identify individuals and their movements

title: Inference of Individual Identity
description: Health Analytics Service P3 can derive daily routine and movement patterns that may indirectly identify individuals even without direct identifiers, through unique behavioral signatures.
assumptions: Movement patterns are unique enough to identify individuals

title: Unauthorized Location Data Disclosure
description: Location history data processed by P3 may be disclosed to unauthorized parties through system compromise, improper access controls, or data sharing without proper consent mechanisms.
assumptions: Inadequate access controls or data sharing policies exist

title: Excessive Location Data Collection
description: Querying location history across multiple sessions to derive daily routines may collect more location data than necessary for the stated purpose, violating data minimization principles.
assumptions: The analytics service collects and processes more location data than minimally required

title: Location Data Usurpation
description: Unauthorized parties may access or manipulate location history data from DS2 through P3, potentially impersonating users or altering movement patterns.
assumptions: Authentication and authorization mechanisms are insufficient

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Health Insights
description: Inferred health-condition risk indicators, routine summaries, and trend flags transmitted from Health Analytics Service to Companion Mobile App could be intercepted or accessed by unauthorized parties during transmission or storage.
assumptions: Data flow lacks adequate encryption or access controls; network or application vulnerabilities exist.

title: Re-identification of Health Data
description: Inferred health insights may contain sufficient detail to identify specific individuals, especially when combined with other data sources or metadata.
assumptions: Health insights include granular or unique health patterns; user identity information may be embedded or inferable.

title: Excessive Health Data Sharing
description: Analytics service may share more detailed health information than necessary for the Companion Mobile App's intended functionality, violating data minimization principles.
assumptions: App requires only high-level summaries, but analytics provides granular inferred insights.

title: Unauthorized Access via App Compromise
description: If Companion Mobile App is compromised or authentication is bypassed, unauthorized users could access sensitive health insights transmitted from analytics service.
assumptions: App has weak authentication or session management; device security is insufficient.

title: Linkability of Health Insights to Other Data
description: Health insights received by the app could be linked to other user data (e.g., location, device ID, usage patterns) to create comprehensive user profiles.
assumptions: App collects additional data that can be correlated with health insights; no data anonymization is applied.

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Sensitive Health Indicators
description: The app dashboard displays inferred condition indicators (eating-disorder or diabetes risk signals) that could be intercepted, leaked, or accessed by unauthorized parties during transmission or storage.
assumptions: Health data is transmitted over network and stored on device/server
uncertainty_note: Node ID D.1.1 is approximate without reference material

title: Re-identification from Health Condition Signals
description: The displayed health indicators (eating-disorder or diabetes risk) could be used to identify the user's medical condition, potentially leading to stigmatization or discrimination if exposed.
assumptions: Health indicators are unique enough to identify user's condition
uncertainty_note: Node ID I.1.1 is approximate without reference material

title: Linkability of Health Data with Other Data Sources
description: The health indicators displayed could be linked with other data (location, usage patterns, other health records) to create a comprehensive profile of the user.
assumptions: Multiple data sources exist that could be correlated
uncertainty_note: Node ID L.1.1 is approximate without reference material

title: Unauthorized Access to User Health Dashboard
description: An attacker could potentially gain unauthorized access to the companion app dashboard and view the user's sensitive health condition indicators.
assumptions: Authentication mechanisms may be compromised
uncertainty_note: Node ID U.1.1 is approximate without reference material

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Health Data
description: Health and location data hosted at the cloud provider could be disclosed to unauthorized third parties through insider threats, compromised access controls, or data breaches.

title: Data Tampering with Health Records
description: Analytics data, models, and health datasets could be altered or corrupted by malicious actors at the cloud provider, compromising data integrity and potentially leading to incorrect health analytics.

title: Data Misuse by Cloud Provider
description: The cloud hosting provider could misuse the full health and location dataset for purposes beyond the agreed scope, such as selling data to third parties or using it for unauthorized profiling.

title: Re-identification of Individuals
description: The combination of health data and location data could enable re-identification of individuals, even if data is anonymized, due to the unique nature of health and location information.

title: Linkability of Health Data
description: Health data hosted at the cloud provider could be linked with other datasets (e.g., government records, commercial data) to create comprehensive profiles of individuals.

title: Regulatory Non-compliance
description: Hosting sensitive health data at a third-party cloud provider may create compliance risks with regulations like HIPAA, GDPR, or other healthcare data protection laws if the provider does not meet required standards.
